thread:
jon (Design): Quick sync — looked at the latest autoscale control mock. want to lock down three tiny things before dev handoff: min/max labeling, how we show 'burst budget' (phrase + tooltip), and the pool fallback ordering affordance. screenshot: https://redwood.design/s/rt-autoscale-mock :point_up:

maya (PM): thanks — nice, i like the compact slider. Q: does burst budget mean the max extra GPUs we can borrow or total GPUs including burst? wording should be explicit for billing teams. :thinking:

lee (Frontend): agreed to be explicit. proposal: label the slider "Burst (temporary capacity)" and a short inline badge "+X GPUs for up to Y mins". that keeps the main UI uncluttered.

jon (Design): i sketched two microcopy variants in the doc: 
- "Burst (extra GPUs, temporary)"
- "Burst budget — extra GPUs available for short surges"
Which reads better for you all?

maya (PM): vote for the second. "budget" hints at a finite resource which is good. also we should show estimated cost delta when users hover.

sam (SRE): on fallback ordering — backend will route to preferred pool then fallback to cheaper preemptible pools. we need a clear UI cue for "fallback order" and whether it's automatic or pinned. current mock hides it behind an overflow menu which feels discoverability-poor.

lee (Frontend): can we try a compact row under pool picker: "Primary > Fallbacks" with chips listing pools and an inline edit icon? that way you can reorder by drag or a simple edit modal. keeps it visible but not huge.

jon (Design): sketch attached: chips with handle, small drag affordance, accessible label "Pool order: primary then fallbacks". also a tooltip: "Requests use primary pool; if unavailable, try next in order."

aisha (A11y): two a11y nits: sliders need aria-valuetext that includes both current value and unit (e.g., "Burst budget: 2 GPUs for 10 minutes"). the drag handle must be keyboard operable and descriptive. also color alone shouldn't indicate preemptible vs reserved — add an icon + text.

lee (Frontend): good call. i will expose aria-valuetext and add a visible label for pool type. we should also ensure keyboard reordering for chips (arrow keys + space to pick up).

jon (Design): another microcopy callout: when min == max we currently show "Fixed capacity". maybe say "Fixed pool size" to avoid confusion with SLO slider. thoughts?

maya (PM): "Fixed pool size" is clearer. also add a small hint line saying "To allow autoscaling, set max > min" with a link to docs. Keeps people from accidentally locking themselves.

sam (SRE): backend caveat: when a pool hits quota, fallback might add latency — we should surface an estimated latency impact in the UI (very small text) so users trade off cost vs latency. e.g., "Fallback may add ~100-250ms per request".

jon (Design): good — i'll add a muted inline cost/latency preview below the selector. small copy: "Estimated cost + latency when using fallbacks".

aisha (A11y): last: ensure the SLO slider labels have focus-visible state and tooltip content is programmatically available. tooltips often disappear for keyboard users. prefer inline help toggles.

lee (Frontend): noted. i'll convert ephemeral tooltips into expand/collapse inline help panels for keyboard users.

maya (PM): checklist for handoff?
- finalize microcopy (jon/maya)
- reorder chips + keyboard reorder (lee)
- aria-valuetext and inline help (aisha)
- fallback latency/cost preview (sam)

jon (Design): will push copy variants to figma and tag everyone. leaving the draft microcopy here for quick reference:
```
Burst budget — extra GPUs available for short surges. Limits how many temporary GPUs can be allocated and for how long.
Primary pool: the preferred GPU pool for this route. Fallback pools: used if primary is exhausted.
Fixed pool size — min and max are the same; autoscaling is disabled.
```

lee (Frontend): thanks, i'll start on the keyboard a11y spikes tomorrow and open a PR for the chips pattern.

deploy-bot: new design file uploaded by jon (Design): https://redwood.design/files/rt-autoscale-v3.fig

maya (PM): great work team. tagging for final comments, otherwise i'll kick off dev tasks tomorrow. :rocket:
